content.overview: Judicial and administrative accountability ensures that holders of public power remain answerable for the lawful exercise of their functions. Judicial accountability operates through constitutional mechanisms of appointment, transfer, removal and in-house processes, while administrative accountability operates through hierarchy, audit, legislative oversight and judicial review.
content.glance: Identify the office and the source of power; locate the accountability mechanism (constitutional, statutory or administrative); and test whether the challenge is maintainable without impairing independence of the judiciary where engaged.
content.study: Accountability is the counterpart of power. For the judiciary, independence and accountability must be balanced: mechanisms such as the constitutional removal process, in-house procedures and transparency measures address misconduct without subordinating judicial decision-making to executive control. For the administration, accountability runs through superior review, audit institutions, legislative committees, ombudsman-type bodies and judicial review. Neither independence nor accountability is absolute; each is structured by the Constitution and statute. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the Constitution and the specific statute. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine; evidence provisions apply only when proof issues arise.

sections.heading: Meaning of Accountability
sections.body: Accountability means answerability for the exercise of public power according to law, with consequences for abuse or neglect of duty.

sections.heading: Judicial Accountability Mechanisms
sections.body: Constitutional removal, in-house procedures, and institutional transparency measures address judicial conduct while preserving decisional independence.

sections.heading: Administrative Accountability
sections.body: Hierarchy, audit, legislative oversight, grievance redress and judicial review keep the administration within legal bounds.

sections.heading: Independence and Accountability Balance
sections.body: Independence protects impartial decision-making; accountability prevents impunity. Both are constitutional values.

sections.heading: Remedies and Limits
sections.body: Challenges must respect institutional competence. Not every grievance about a judgment is a matter of judicial accountability.

provisions.title: Supreme Court — composition and removal framework

examples.title: Conduct versus outcome
examples.body: Disagreement with a judgment is not by itself a failure of judicial accountability. Accountability mechanisms address conduct and process.

examples.title: Administrative audit failure
examples.body: Persistent failure of internal audit and hierarchical control over a department raises administrative accountability issues distinct from judicial review of a single order.

hypotheticals.question: Does every unpopular judgment prove lack of judicial accountability?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Accountability mechanisms address conduct and process, not mere disagreement with outcomes.

hypotheticals.question: Does independence mean the judiciary is unaccountable?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Independence and accountability coexist under the Constitution.

distinctions.title: Judicial accountability vs appeal on merits
distinctions.left: Accountability concerns conduct and institutional answerability.
distinctions.right: Appeal redecides the correctness of a judgment on law and fact.

misconceptions.trap: Any unpopular judgment proves lack of judicial accountability.
misconceptions.correction: Accountability mechanisms address conduct and process, not mere disagreement with outcomes.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should an accountability problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the office and power. II. Locate the accountability mechanism. III. Test independence constraints. IV. Assess maintainability. V. Formulate proportionate institutional response.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify the office; state the mechanism; address independence; seek only maintainable relief.
